# quality.font-count — A page pulls in too many font files

- **Check ID:** `quality.font-count`
- **Default severity:** `warning`; users can override it in `seaworthy.config.json`.
- **Needs:** `html`, `files`
- **Standards:** none
- **Source module:** `packages/verify/src/checks/font-count.ts`
- **Prose page:** [`docs/checks/quality.font-count.md`](../quality.font-count.md) — embedded below verbatim; write it there, never here.

One page pulls in more distinct font files than the maximum allows.

## Why it matters

Every font file is another request the browser must make before the page can show its text, and font requests are the ones people notice: the words reflow or blink in as each file lands. A page that ships eight or ten font files is usually one design system applied blindly — a family in five weights plus a second family plus an icon font — and each file is bytes nobody chose deliberately. Two families across a handful of weights is what a page genuinely needs, so the default maximum is 6 distinct font files per page: room for a text family and a display family with their usual weights, and a finding for anything beyond that. Agents reading the site pay the same cost per request, so a page heavy in font files is a slower site for everyone.

## What it checks

For each page, with no browser and no network, the check collects the distinct font files the build ships that the page pulls in:

- through `<link rel="stylesheet">` elements whose target is a stylesheet in the built site — every `url(...)` in that stylesheet's text is resolved against the stylesheet's own path, and
- through the page's inline `<style>` blocks, resolved against the page's own path.

`@import` chains inside a stylesheet are not followed, exactly as in `quality.page-weight`; that stays a follow-up.

A URL counts as a font when its path (with any query string or fragment stripped) ends in `.woff`, `.woff2`, `.ttf`, `.otf`, or `.eot` — the same extension set `quality.page-weight` sums under its fonts bucket. Files are deduplicated by their resolved site path, so the same font referenced by two stylesheets, or the same file twice with different cache-busting queries, counts once. A page is reported once when its distinct count exceeds the maximum; a page at the maximum is silent.

Only files the build serves are counted. A `url()` at a font that is not in the built site is `assets.missing`'s finding, not this check's; an external CDN font is not the build's file; a data URI travels with the CSS itself. None of them add to the count.

The location depends on where the count comes from: when any counted font arrives through a linked stylesheet, the finding sits at the page's `<head>`; when only inline `<style>` carries fonts, it sits at the first such `<style>` element. The message names the count, the maximum, and every offending font path in sorted order.

## How to fix

The finding lists the font files, so cut them where the `@font-face` rules are written — the CSS source or the site's font pipeline, not the built output:

```css
/* before: four static weights of one family, four files */
@font-face{font-family:Body;src:url(/fonts/body-light.woff2)}
@font-face{font-family:Body;src:url(/fonts/body-regular.woff2)}
@font-face{font-family:Body;src:url(/fonts/body-medium.woff2)}
@font-face{font-family:Body;src:url(/fonts/body-bold.woff2)}
```

```css
/* after: one self-hosted variable font covers all four weights */
@font-face{font-family:Body;src:url(/fonts/body-variable.woff2) format("woff2-variations");font-weight:300 700}
```

Drop weights and families no text on the page uses, subset each font to the glyphs the page actually renders, or replace several static weights with one variable font. Do not delete `@font-face` rules at random from the built CSS: the fix belongs in the source that generates it.

## Options

Under `checks."quality.font-count".options`, the check accepts `max`: the number of distinct font files one page may pull in. A whole number of at least 1; the default is `6`. A value that is not an integer, is below 1, or is not a number at all falls back to the default — the same way `quality.page-weight`'s budgets and `images.size`'s `maxBytes` do — so a typo in the config never turns the check off or crashes a run.

```json
{ "checks": { "quality.font-count": { "options": { "max": 4 } } } }
```

## Standards

None.
